description: Half A of CAM-111: additive dev-container isolation artifact (Dockerfile + egress firewall + devcontainer.json + Docker preflight helper + ADR/docs), zero change to live worker-spawn behavior.

officialDocsConsulted.summary: Reference devcontainer = devcontainer.json + Dockerfile + init-firewall.sh. Firewall needs NET_ADMIN+NET_RAW via runArgs. remoteUser must be non-root (CLI rejects --dangerously-skip-permissions as root). Pin CLI via npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code@X.Y.Z + DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER=1 instead of the auto-updating feature. Persist ~/.claude via a named volume. Do NOT mount ~/.ssh or host cred files; use repo-scoped/short-lived tokens.

Egress allowlist for Claude Code: api.anthropic.com, claude.ai, platform.claude.com, raw.githubusercontent.com. downloads.claude.ai and storage.googleapis.com are NOT needed when the CLI is npm-installed and pinned. WebFetch preflight still hits api.anthropic.com unless skipWebFetchPreflight is set. Add github.com and package registries (registry.npmjs.org) for git and build.

userStories.title: Add pinned non-root worker Dockerfile
userStories.description: As a cam operator, I need a .devcontainer/Dockerfile that defines the worker base image (bun + git + node), installs a pinned Claude Code CLI as a non-root user, and disables the auto-updater, so that the future containerized worker runs a reproducible, isolation-ready image.
acceptanceCriteria: A new file .devcontainer/Dockerfile exists. [oracle: file-assert test -f .devcontainer/Dockerfile]

The Dockerfile installs the Claude Code CLI pinned to an exact version via npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code@2.1.197 (no floating tag). [oracle: grep -Eq 'npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code@2\.1\.197' .devcontainer/Dockerfile]
The Dockerfile sets DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER so the pinned CLI never auto-updates. [oracle: grep -q 'DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER' .devcontainer/Dockerfile]

The Dockerfile provides bun and git in the image (base image or explicit install). [oracle: file-assert grep -Eq 'bun|oven/bun|BUN_' .devcontainer/Dockerfile && grep -q 'git' .devcontainer/Dockerfile]

The Dockerfile creates and switches to a NON-ROOT user via a USER directive that is not root (e.g. USER node), because the Claude Code CLI rejects --dangerously-skip-permissions when launched as root. [oracle: grep -Eq '^USER (?!root)[A-Za-z]' .devcontainer/Dockerfile]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
Full quality spine passes including biome lint, knip, jscpd, file-size, and coverage ratchets (bun run check:all). [oracle: bun run check:all]
userStories.notes: New file: .devcontainer/Dockerfile (additive; no existing devcontainer dir, this creates it). Pin the CLI to the version currently installed/current: @anthropic-ai/claude-code@2.1.197 (verified via `npm view @anthropic-ai/claude-code version` and `claude --version` on 2026-07-01). Official-doc facts to re-check (relatedDoc: officialDocsConsulted 'Claude Code dev containers'): the docs explicitly say to pin via `npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code@X.Y.Z` AND set DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER=1 INSTEAD of the auto-updating Dev Container Feature; remoteUser/USER must be non-root (CLI rejects bypass as root). Keep this image minimal (Simplicity First): bun + git + node + pinned CLI + non-root user only; no speculative tools. This is a plain Dockerfile, NOT a .ts source file, so no biome/knip/coverage impact and no vendor/templates touch (embed-vendor:check NOT required). CI is macos-latest with NO Docker: do NOT add any criterion that builds or runs the image. .devcontainer/ is a project-domain file, not cam-harness state, so it lives at repo root not under scripts/cam/.

userStories.title: Add egress default-deny firewall script
userStories.description: As a cam operator, I need a .devcontainer/init-firewall.sh that enforces default-deny egress and allowlists EXACTLY the domains the worker needs, so that a containerized worker running under bypass can only reach Anthropic, GitHub, and the package registry.
acceptanceCriteria: A new file .devcontainer/init-firewall.sh exists and is a shell script (has a shebang). [oracle: file-assert test -f .devcontainer/init-firewall.sh && head -1 .devcontainer/init-firewall.sh | grep -q '#!/']

The script allowlists EXACTLY these egress domains and no others: api.anthropic.com, claude.ai, platform.claude.com, github.com, *.github.com, registry.npmjs.org, raw.githubusercontent.com. [oracle: file-assert grep -q 'api.anthropic.com' .devcontainer/init-firewall.sh && grep -q 'claude.ai' .devcontainer/init-firewall.sh && grep -q 'platform.claude.com' .devcontainer/init-firewall.sh && grep -q 'github.com' .devcontainer/init-firewall.sh && grep -q 'registry.npmjs.org' .devcontainer/init-firewall.sh && grep -q 'raw.githubusercontent.com' .devcontainer/init-firewall.sh]

The allowlist has NO 8th domain: the allowed domains are declared in a single dedicated allowlist block (e.g. an ALLOWED_DOMAINS bash array or a here-doc) and the count of domain string-literals in that block equals exactly 7, so a stray extra domain fails the check. [oracle: reviewer-judgment (the dedicated allowlist block contains exactly the 7 named domains and no others: api.anthropic.com, claude.ai, platform.claude.com, github.com, *.github.com, registry.npmjs.org, raw.githubusercontent.com) + file-assert (the count of domain entries in the allowlist array/here-doc equals 7)]

The script does NOT allowlist downloads.claude.ai or storage.googleapis.com (not needed for an npm-installed pinned CLI, per network-config docs). [oracle: file-assert ! grep -q 'downloads.claude.ai' .devcontainer/init-firewall.sh && ! grep -q 'storage.googleapis.com' .devcontainer/init-firewall.sh]
The default policy is deny (drop) with the allowlist as the only exception. [oracle: file-assert grep -Eiq 'DROP|default.?deny|-P OUTPUT DROP' .devcontainer/init-firewall.sh]

The script is idempotent (safe to re-run: flushes/resets its own rules before applying, e.g. iptables -F on its chain). [oracle: file-assert grep -Eq 'iptables .*-F|flush' .devcontainer/init-firewall.sh]
The script includes a self-verify step that confirms an allowed domain is reachable and a blocked domain is not (fails loudly if the ruleset is wrong). [oracle: reviewer-judgment]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
Full quality spine passes (bun run check:all). [oracle: bun run check:all]
userStories.notes: New file: .devcontainer/init-firewall.sh (additive shell script). Model on the Anthropic reference init-firewall.sh (github.com/anthropics/claude-code/blob/main/.devcontainer/init-firewall.sh) but TRIM the allowlist to EXACTLY the seven domains the operator specified: api.anthropic.com, claude.ai, platform.claude.com, github.com, *.github.com, registry.npmjs.org, raw.githubusercontent.com. Put those seven in ONE dedicated allowlist block (a bash ALLOWED_DOMAINS array or a here-doc) so the exact-count oracle can verify there is no stray 8th domain. Official-doc facts to re-check (officialDocsConsulted 'Claude Code network config'): api.anthropic.com/claude.ai/platform.claude.com/raw.githubusercontent.com are the Anthropic-side needs; github.com covers git push/fetch; registry.npmjs.org covers the npm CLI install; downloads.claude.ai + storage.googleapis.com are explicitly NOT needed for a pinned npm CLI (do not add them). The firewall needs NET_ADMIN+NET_RAW (granted in US-003 devcontainer.json runArgs). Do NOT run iptables in any test or CI step: CI is macos-latest with no Docker and no root; the live-firewall smoke is an operator/local ceremony, not a CI gate. Verification here is file-assert grep for the exact domain set plus a count-equals-7 assert on the allowlist block. Not a .ts file and not under vendor/templates: no biome/knip/embed-vendor impact.

userStories.title: Add devcontainer.json wiring the image, firewall, and non-root user
userStories.description: As a cam operator, I need a .devcontainer/devcontainer.json that references the Dockerfile, grants the firewall its capabilities, runs as a non-root user, persists ~/.claude, sets the isolation env vars, and runs init-firewall.sh on container start, so that the three artifacts compose into a working isolation boundary.
acceptanceCriteria: A new file .devcontainer/devcontainer.json exists and is valid JSON (JSONC comments stripped parse cleanly, or it is strict JSON). [oracle: bun -e "JSON.parse(require('node:fs').readFileSync('.devcontainer/devcontainer.json','utf8').replace(/\\/\\*[\\s\\S]*?\\*\\//g,'').replace(/(^|[^:])\\/\\/.*$/gm,'$1'))"]

devcontainer.json references the local Dockerfile via a build.dockerfile (not a prebuilt image feature). [oracle: file-assert grep -q 'Dockerfile' .devcontainer/devcontainer.json && grep -q 'dockerfile' .devcontainer/devcontainer.json]

runArgs grants BOTH --cap-add=NET_ADMIN and --cap-add=NET_RAW so the firewall can install iptables rules. [oracle: file-assert grep -q 'NET_ADMIN' .devcontainer/devcontainer.json && grep -q 'NET_RAW' .devcontainer/devcontainer.json]

remoteUser is set to a non-root user (matches the Dockerfile USER, e.g. node), because the CLI rejects bypass as root. [oracle: file-assert grep -Eq '"remoteUser"\\s*:\\s*"(?!root)' .devcontainer/devcontainer.json]

A named volume mount targets the remoteUser's ~/.claude to persist auth/settings across rebuilds. [oracle: file-assert grep -q '.claude' .devcontainer/devcontainer.json && grep -Eq 'type=volume|"type"\\s*:\\s*"volume"' .devcontainer/devcontainer.json]

containerEnv sets DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER and CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC. [oracle: file-assert grep -q 'DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER' .devcontainer/devcontainer.json && grep -q 'CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC' .devcontainer/devcontainer.json]

A postCreate or postStart lifecycle hook runs init-firewall.sh. [oracle: file-assert grep -Eq 'postCreate|postStart' .devcontainer/devcontainer.json && grep -q 'init-firewall.sh' .devcontainer/devcontainer.json]

The devcontainer.json does NOT mount host ~/.ssh or host credential files (only the named ~/.claude volume + the repo workspace). [oracle: file-assert ! grep -q '.ssh' .devcontainer/devcontainer.json]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
Full quality spine passes (bun run check:all). [oracle: bun run check:all]
userStories.notes: New file: .devcontainer/devcontainer.json. Depends on US-001 (Dockerfile) and US-002 (init-firewall.sh). Official-doc facts to re-check (officialDocsConsulted 'Claude Code dev containers'): firewall capabilities NET_ADMIN+NET_RAW go in runArgs; remoteUser must be non-root; persist ~/.claude via a named volume (docs example: source=claude-code-config,target=/home/node/.claude,type=volume; the reference uses ${devcontainerId} to isolate per project); containerEnv is where DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER=1 + CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC=1 go; do NOT mount host ~/.ssh or cred files (use repo-scoped/short-lived tokens; that token wiring is Half B / CAM-150, NOT this story). The devcontainer.json JSON-parse oracle strips // and /* */ comments before JSON.parse because devcontainer.json is conventionally JSONC. CI is macos-latest with no Docker: do NOT add any criterion that runs `devcontainer up` or docker. Not a .ts file, not under vendor/templates: no embed-vendor impact.

userStories.title: Add tested Docker preflight helper (uncalled)
userStories.description: As a cam operator, I need a preflightWorkerContainer() helper in src/supervisor/ that checks the Docker daemon is reachable AND the worker image is built/current and returns a structured result, unit-tested with mocked docker calls, so that the future Half-B spawn rewrite can gate dispatch on container readiness.
acceptanceCriteria: A new file src/supervisor/preflight-container.ts exports preflightWorkerContainer that accepts an injectable spawn/docker-probe dependency (no real daemon shell-out at import time). [oracle: file-assert grep -q 'export function preflightWorkerContainer' src/supervisor/preflight-container.ts]

preflightWorkerContainer returns a structured result (a discriminated union or an object with an ok/ready boolean and a reason field) distinguishing daemon-unreachable from image-missing/stale. [oracle: file-assert grep -Eq 'daemon|reachable' src/supervisor/preflight-container.ts && grep -Eq 'image' src/supervisor/preflight-container.ts]

The helper is NOT wired into the dispatch path (worker-argv.ts / host.ts / loop.ts remain untouched); it is a tested-but-uncalled exported helper (safe because knip treats test files as entry points). [oracle: file-assert ! grep -rq 'preflightWorkerContainer' src/supervisor/host.ts src/supervisor/loop.ts src/supervisor/worker-argv.ts]

A unit test at test/supervisor/preflight-container.test.ts covers: daemon reachable + image current => ready; daemon unreachable => not-ready with a daemon reason; image missing/stale => not-ready with an image reason. The test injects a fake docker-probe (mock); it does NOT shell out to a real Docker daemon. [oracle: file-assert test -f test/supervisor/preflight-container.test.ts && grep -Eq 'preflightWorkerContainer' test/supervisor/preflight-container.test.ts]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass, including the new preflight test (bun test). [oracle: bun test]

Full quality spine passes: biome lint clean, knip finds no new dead code (the exported helper is reachable via the test entry point), jscpd under threshold, file-size within budget, coverage ratchet holds (bun run check:all). [oracle: bun run check:all]
userStories.notes: New files: src/supervisor/preflight-container.ts + test/supervisor/preflight-container.test.ts. This maps to issue acceptance criterion 9 (preflight checks Docker available + worker image built/current before dispatch), but WIRING it into dispatch is Half B (CAM-150): do NOT touch src/supervisor/worker-argv.ts or host.ts spawn logic. Follow the injectable-dep pattern used across the codebase (patterns.md: makeNotifyOrchestrator factory, sidecar-pid signal-0 probe, makeReadWorkerReport null-on-error). Inject the docker-probe as a dependency (e.g. a `probe: (args: string[]) => { stdout: string; exitCode: number }` seam) so the unit test asserts behavior with a fake and never touches a real daemon (CI is macos-latest with NO Docker). Structured result: discriminated union { ready: true } | { ready: false; reason: 'daemon-unreachable' | 'image-missing' | 'image-stale' } mirrors the { ok:false; reason } union pattern in patterns.md (US-005 CAM-86). Docker daemon probe idiom: `docker info` exit 0 = reachable; `docker image inspect <tag>` exit 0 = built. Guard noUncheckedIndexedAccess on any argv/regex parse. knip: an exported-but-uncalled function is fine because test/**/*.ts is a knip entry point (patterns.md knip grandfathering bullet). The real image-build + live preflight against a running daemon is an operator/local ceremony, NOT part of this story's oracles.

The ADR justifies all three ADR gates (hard-to-reverse, surprising-without-context, real trade-off) and names the alternatives considered: native bash-sandbox, sandbox-runtime, VM, and cloud-Daytona.
